about.title: A student-led catalog for the Cornell Tech MakerLab.
about.intro: MakerLab Tools is the inventory and assistant for the Cornell Tech MakerLab. It helps students browse every machine and hand tool, see which units are available, read the manuals and safety requirements, and ask how to use a tool in their own language before they walk over.
about.origin: The project began as a weekend prototype on a Notion catalog and now runs on its own database. Staff and SuperMakers edit tools, work maintenance tickets, and review corrections right in the app, and an optional mirror keeps a read-only copy in Notion for anyone who prefers it there.
about.builtByBody: Isaac Steinberg, Johnson Cornell Tech MBA '26. Built as a student-led project to make it easier for the MakerLab community to find and safely use the lab's equipment.
about.howItWorksBody: The front end is a Next.js 16 app on Vercel, with Postgres for the catalog and Blob storage for photos and archived manuals. New equipment is identified from a photo in the chat, researched in the background against the manufacturer's own pages, and published only after a staff member reviews it. The assistant answers from the catalog and each tool's manuals, and says so when it doesn't know.
about.feedbackBody: If you spot a mistake, use "Report a correction" on the tool's page — corrections go to the staff queue and are fixed in the app. For a broken machine, use Report in the header.
about.mcpBody: The catalog is also available to AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Codex over MCP, at this site's /api/mcp address. Browsing needs no account. To let an assistant file reports as you, with your role's permissions and nothing more, sign in with Google from the assistant; a personal access token is there for clients that can't.

account.title: Connect an AI assistant
account.lede: Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Codex or another MCP client to MakerLab Tools. The easiest way is to sign in with Google: the assistant acts as you, with your role's permissions and nothing more. Browsing needs no account.
account.unavailable: Your tokens could not be loaded right now. Try again shortly.
account.signedOut: Sign in here to create a personal access token. You only need one for a client or script that can't sign in with Google.

signIn.heading: Sign in with Google (recommended)
signIn.body: Give your assistant this address. It sends you here to sign in with Google and approve the connection. There's no token to copy or keep safe, and you can disconnect it from this page at any time.
signIn.claudeCodeThen: Then run /mcp in Claude Code, choose makerlab and pick Authenticate. Your browser opens to sign in.
signIn.codexAgain: If your browser doesn't open to sign in, or to sign in again later, run:
signIn.connectorsBody: Go to Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector and paste the address above. Menu names can change between releases.
signIn.chatgptBody: Create a custom connector (under Settings → Connectors, or developer mode, depending on your plan) with the address above and OAuth authentication.
signIn.readOnlyNote: On the approval page you can choose read-only if the assistant only needs to look things up.

account.endpointBody: To look things up without signing in, add this address instead. It offers the public, read-only tools.
account.safetyBody: A token acts as you. Make one per device, prefer read-only, and revoke it here if a laptop is lost. Anything an assistant changes in the catalog arrives as a proposal that staff accept in the app.

tokens.heading: Personal access tokens
tokens.lede: Use these for a client or script that can't sign in with Google, for example Claude Desktop's config file, a CI job or your own script. A token acts as you until it expires or you revoke it.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.nameHint: Name it after the device or app, so you know which one to revoke.
tokens.readOnlyHint: The assistant can look things up, but can't file reports or change anything.
tokens.revealWarning: Copy it now. It won't be shown again, and anyone who has it can act as you.
tokens.setupEnv: Put the token in an environment variable, for example in your shell profile, so it stays out of config files and chats:
tokens.revokeConfirm: Revoke {name}? Anything using it stops working at once.

errors.rate_limited: Too many changes at once. Wait a minute and try again.
errors.invalid_field: Give the token a name (up to 80 characters) and choose when it expires.
errors.too_many_tokens: You have too many active tokens. Revoke one you no longer use first.
errors.not_found: That token isn't yours or no longer exists.
errors.failed: That didn't work. Try again shortly.

warnings.audit_unavailable: Done, but the change couldn't be recorded in the audit trail.

apps.heading: Connected apps
apps.lede: Apps you connected by signing in to MakerLab with OAuth, such as claude.ai or ChatGPT.
apps.revokeConfirm: Disconnect {name}? It stops working at once and has to sign in again.

oauth.signInBody: {client} wants to connect to MakerLab Tools as you. Sign in with your {institution} account to continue.
oauth.signInUnconfigured: Sign-in isn't set up on this deployment yet.
oauth.consentTitle: {client} wants to access MakerLab Tools as you
oauth.consentBody: It will act as {name}, with the tools your role ({role}) allows.
oauth.consentSafety: Nothing it does publishes or edits the catalog without a person accepting it in the app. You can disconnect it at any time from Connect an AI assistant in your profile menu.
oauth.consentSignedOut: Sign in first, then start the connection again from the app.
oauth.readOnlyHint: Let it look things up, but not file reports or change anything.
oauth.expired: This request has expired or isn't yours. Start the connection again from the app.
oauth.failed: That didn't work. Start the connection again from the app.
